title: Build an agent harness like DeepSeek Harness
topic: LLM agent harness architecture, modelled on DeepSeek Harness
summary: Starting from what a language model is, you build a complete agent harness piece by piece: model calls, tools, the agent loop, an event log, provider adapters, plugins, safe tools, a sandbox, context management, subagents and a front end. Every design choice is checked against how the open-source DeepSeek Harness actually does it, and you write a small working version of each part in TypeScript.

concepts.name: Language model
concepts.summary: A program that repeatedly predicts the most likely next piece of text.

concepts.name: Token
concepts.summary: Models read and write text as small numbered chunks called tokens.

concepts.name: Context window
concepts.summary: A model can only consider a fixed number of tokens in one request.

concepts.name: Model API call
concepts.summary: Your program sends text to a hosted model as an HTTP request and gets text back.

concepts.name: Message roles
concepts.summary: A chat request is a list of messages, each labelled system, user or assistant.

concepts.name: Stateless model
concepts.summary: The model remembers nothing between requests, so each one carries the whole conversation.

concepts.name: Streaming
concepts.summary: The reply can arrive in small pieces as it is generated.

concepts.name: Stop reason
concepts.summary: Every reply ends with a label saying why the model stopped.

concepts.name: Tool schema
concepts.summary: You describe each function the model may request with a name, a description and a JSON Schema.

concepts.name: Tool call
concepts.summary: Instead of text, the model can reply with a structured request to run one of your functions.

concepts.name: Tool result
concepts.summary: Your program runs the function and sends the outcome back, matched to the request by its id.

concepts.name: Agent loop
concepts.summary: Repeating model request, tool run and tool result until the model answers in plain text.

concepts.name: Turn
concepts.summary: One complete answer to the user, made of one or more model requests called steps.

concepts.name: Step limit
concepts.summary: A maximum number of steps per turn so a confused model cannot loop forever.

concepts.name: Tool error result
concepts.summary: A failed tool still returns a result, marked as an error, so the model can recover.

concepts.name: Event log
concepts.summary: Recording every fact in order and never changing a recorded fact.

concepts.name: Session event
concepts.summary: The typed facts an agent records: turns, steps, messages, tool calls and results.

concepts.name: Derived history
concepts.summary: The messages sent to the model are rebuilt by reading the event log.

concepts.name: JSONL file
concepts.summary: Storing the log as a file with one JSON event per line, written in batches.

concepts.name: Session resume
concepts.summary: Reading the file back after a restart and continuing where the conversation stopped.

concepts.name: Orphaned tool call
concepts.summary: A tool request with no recorded result must get a synthetic error result before the model sees it again.

concepts.name: Stream chunk
concepts.summary: A small typed union of pieces any provider's streamed reply can be translated into.

concepts.name: Message assembler
concepts.summary: Code that joins stream chunks into one finished message, including half-written tool requests.

concepts.name: Model adapter
concepts.summary: One interface with a single stream method that hides each provider's wire format.

concepts.name: Reasoning block
concepts.summary: Thinking models stream their working-out as a separate kind of content.

concepts.name: Retry with backoff
concepts.summary: Retrying failed model requests after growing waits, and recording every attempt.

concepts.name: Cancellation
concepts.summary: Stopping a request or tool cleanly when the user changes their mind.

concepts.name: Plugin
concepts.summary: A self-contained piece of code that adds one feature to a host program.

concepts.name: Disposer
concepts.summary: Every registration a plugin makes returns a function that undoes it, run when the plugin unloads.

concepts.name: Service
concepts.summary: A named object one plugin provides for others to use, removed when its plugin unloads.

concepts.name: Service injection
concepts.summary: A plugin declares the services it needs and only starts once they exist.

concepts.name: Event hook
concepts.summary: Plugins register listeners that run when another part of the program announces something.

concepts.name: Waterfall hook
concepts.summary: Listeners wrap one decision in turn, each choosing to pass it on or decide it themselves.

concepts.name: Config rows
concepts.summary: The whole application is a list of plugin rows that layered patch files can change by id.

concepts.name: Agent scope
concepts.summary: Registrations made for one agent are visible only to it and removed with it.

concepts.name: Tool registry
concepts.summary: A service that holds every tool and gives the model only their schemas.

concepts.name: Argument validation
concepts.summary: Checking the model's tool arguments against the schema and returning clear errors.

concepts.name: Tool pipeline
concepts.summary: A fixed sequence of hooks before and after every tool runs, with each call and result logged.

concepts.name: Approval
concepts.summary: Pausing a risky tool call to ask the person, where anything but a clear yes means no.

concepts.name: Parallel tool calls
concepts.summary: Running requests marked safe at the same time while keeping results in order.

concepts.name: Output spill
concepts.summary: Saving a huge tool result to a file and showing the model only its start, end and location.

concepts.name: Safe file edit
concepts.summary: Editing by replacing one exact match, only after reading the file, written atomically.

concepts.name: Sandbox
concepts.summary: An operating-system fence that limits what a command can change.

concepts.name: Write roots
concepts.summary: The few folders a fenced command is still allowed to change.

concepts.name: Sandbox runner
concepts.summary: Wrapping a command's argument list in Seatbelt on macOS or bubblewrap on Linux.

concepts.name: Failing closed
concepts.summary: Refusing to run a command at all when no working fence is available.

concepts.name: Sandbox escalation
concepts.summary: The model asks, with a reason, to widen the fence for a single retry.

concepts.name: Prompt sections
concepts.summary: The system prompt is assembled from ordered sections that plugins and tools register.

concepts.name: Project instructions
concepts.summary: A repository's own instruction files are added to the conversation as a recorded message.

concepts.name: Prompt caching
concepts.summary: Providers reuse work for a request's unchanged beginning, so history should only grow at the end.

concepts.name: Token budget
concepts.summary: Counting tokens to know when the context window is nearly full.

concepts.name: Compaction
concepts.summary: Replacing old history with a structured summary when the budget runs out.

concepts.name: Surface replacement
concepts.summary: Summarized events stay in the log but are hidden from the model's view of it.

concepts.name: Skill
concepts.summary: A named instruction file the model sees only by name until it asks to load it.

concepts.name: MCP client
concepts.summary: Connecting to external tool servers and registering their tools beside your own.

concepts.name: Agent inbox
concepts.summary: Queued messages that start a new turn or join the current one.

concepts.name: Subagent
concepts.summary: A child agent with its own log, started by a tool call to do one task.

concepts.name: Subagent result
concepts.summary: The child's final answer arrives in the parent's inbox and wakes it.

concepts.name: Depth limit
concepts.summary: A cap on how many levels of agents can start other agents.

concepts.name: Background job
concepts.summary: A long command keeps running and its completion arrives later as a message.

concepts.name: Live event stream
concepts.summary: Front ends subscribe to recorded events and stream pieces to show progress.

concepts.name: Headless runner
concepts.summary: Running one task with no interface and exiting when every agent is idle.

concepts.name: Web gateway
concepts.summary: A browser sends prompts over HTTP and follows progress on one WebSocket.

concepts.name: JSON-RPC over stdio
concepts.summary: Another program drives the harness by exchanging JSON messages on its standard input and output.

concepts.name: The whole harness
concepts.summary: Following one request through every part you built, end to end.
